from urllib.robotparser import RobotFileParser
rp = RobotFileParser()
rp.set_url(base + "robots.txt")
rp.read()
rp.can_fetch("*", base)   # True

headers = {"User-Agent": "LTV-Academy-class-demo (learning exercise)"}
resp = requests.get(base, headers=headers, timeout=10)
caption: Practicing on Books to Scrape — a sandbox built for people learning this. Never assume a real site is.

code:
soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "html.parser")
cards = soup.select("article.product_pod")   # 20 matches

c = cards[0]
c.h3.a["title"]                            # 'A Light in the Attic'
c.select_one("p.price_color").get_text()  # '£51.77'
caption: select() returns every match, select_one() the first. ["attr"] reads an attribute; get_text() the visible text.
Every column comes back as text — the same Chapter 5 cleaning skills apply next.

df["price"] = pd.to_numeric(df["price"].str.replace(r"[^0-9.]", "", regex=True))

import time
for n in (1, 2, 3):
    r = requests.get(f"{base}catalogue/page-{n}.html", headers=headers, timeout=10)
    r.raise_for_status()
    time.sleep(1)   # be gentle
caption: 60 books total across 3 pages here — pause between requests with time.sleep.
